postings.title: Call for Applications: Grant Making Panel (GMP) // Convocatoria de Solicitudes:
postings.descriptionText:
[El texto en español se encuentra a continuación]

1. Call for new GMP members
The International Trans Fund (ITF) is seeking applications from committed activists to be members of its Grant Making Panel (GMP). Applicants may be based and organize within any region of the world.

2. About the ITF
The International Trans Fund (ITF) is a participatory grantmaking fund led by trans activists and donors. We resource trans-led groups globally to advance human rights, self-determination, well-being, and movement power. We have a specific focus on supporting groups with limited access to funding.

3. Role of the GMP
The GMP reviews eligible applications and makes funding decisions consistent with ITF’s mission, values, and priorities. Decisions of the GMP are final, pending Board ratification.
The key responsibilities of the Grant Making Panel are to:

• Participate in online GMP training.

• Join one annual 6-day in-person meeting (location varies) or a virtual equivalent.

• Take part in online discussions and at least 75% of scheduled online meetings.

• Lead grantmaking tasks:

• Encourage trans communities to apply.

• Review, score, and provide feedback on applications.

• Make collective funding decisions.

• Recommend grantmaking priorities and advise on strategy as relevant.

• Strictly uphold ITF confidentiality and conflict-of-interest policies.

4. Profile of the Activists we are Seeking
Before deciding to apply, please confirm that:

• You are committed to advancing trans rights and building sustainable trans movements.

• Your peers consider you credible and trustworthy.

• You value participatory grantmaking and collective, movement-accountable decision-making.

5. What “trans” means at ITF
We use “trans” as a political term for people whose gender identity or expression differs from their sex assigned at birth, including binary and non-binary identities and culturally specific identities worldwide. We do not privilege any identity or terminology over another.

6. Time Commitment

• Annual training: 3–5 hours.

• Application review: 30–50 applications over ~6 weeks (~50 hours/year).

• Annual meeting: 6 days + travel (in-person or virtual).

7. Candidate Qualifications

Essential

• Identify as trans (refer to item 5 above).

• Minimum 3 years of direct trans activism, ideally as a regional and/or international level.

• Recognized by trans activists in your region as a community activist/leader.

• Fluency (spoken and written) in English or Spanish.

• Able and willing to work in a diverse environment (activists and donors).

• Passport enabling international travel (for in-person meetings).

• Reliable in meeting tasks and deadlines.

• Experience managing and reporting on grants for trans work.

8. Conflict of Interest
GMP members (and immediate family members) may not be significantly involved in any group applying to ITF during their tenure and may not benefit financially from assessed or existing ITF grants (See ITF Conflict of Interest Policy). Please note that this means that if you are part of/involved in an organization and selected as a member of the GMP, the organization will not be eligible to apply for grants during their tenure.

9. Term & Compensation

• Term: Three (3) years, appointed by the Board.

• Compensation:USD $1,500 per one-year grant cycle, plus covered travel and per diem for ITF meetings.

10. Selection Process
The Board will appoint seven activists with attention to diversity across gender identities/expressions and inclusion of further-marginalized groups within trans communities. We highly encourage trans men and trans masculine folks to apply.

11. How to Apply
Please submit an application in BambooHR by November 30, 2026.
We intend to inform all candidates of our decisions by January 2027.

//
1. Convocatoria para nuevas personas integrantes del PCA
El Fondo Internacional Trans (FIT) busca activistas comprometides para formar parte de su Panel de Concesión de Apoyos (PCA) . Las personas solicitantes pueden residir y organizarse en cualquier región del mundo.

2. Acerca del FIT
El Fondo Internacional Trans (FIT) es un fondo participativo de apoyos financieros liderado por activistas trans y donantes que lo apoyan. Proporcionamos recursos a grupos liderados por personas trans en todo el mundo para promover los derechos humanos, la autodeterminación, el bienestar y el empoderamiento de los movimientos, especialmente para aquellos grupos con acceso limitado a financiación.

3. Función del PCA
El PCA revisa las solicitudes que cumplen los requisitos y toma decisiones de financiamiento acordes con la misión, los valores y las prioridades de FIT. Las decisiones del PCA son definitivas, a la espera de la ratificación de la junta directiva.
Las principales responsabilidades del panel de concesión de apoyos son:

• Participar en la capacitación en línea del PCA.

• Participar en una reunión anual presencial de 6 días (la ubicación varía) o en su equivalente virtual.

• Participar en los debates en línea y en al menos el 75% de las reuniones en línea programadas.

• Liderar las tareas de concesión de apoyos financieros:

• Alentar a las comunidades trans a presentar una solicitud.

• Revisar, calificar y proporcionar comentarios sobre las solicitudes.

• Tomar decisiones colectivas sobre el financiamiento.

• Recomendar prioridades en la concesión de apoyos financieros y asesorar sobre la estrategia pertinente.

• Respetar estrictamente las políticas de confidencialidad y de conflicto de intereses del FIT.

4. Perfil de las personas activistas que buscamos
Antes de decidirse a presentar su solicitud, confirme que:

• Tienes compromiso con el avance de los derechos de las personas trans y la construcción de movimientos trans sostenibles.

• Tus pares te consideran una persona creíble y digna de confianza.

• Valoras la concesión participativa de apoyos financieros y la toma de decisiones colectiva y responsable ante el movimiento.

5. ¿Qué significa “trans” para el FIT?
Usamos “trans” como término político para referirnos a las personas cuya identidad o expresión de género difiere del sexo que se les asignó al nacer, incluyendo identidades binarias y no binarias, así como identidades culturalmente específicas en todo el mundo. No privilegiamos ninguna identidad ni terminología sobre otra.

6. Compromiso de tiempo

• Capacitación anual: 3-5 horas.

• Revisión de solicitudes: entre 30 y 50 solicitudes durante aproximadamente 6 semanas ( aproximadamente 50 horas al año ).

• Reunión anual: 6 días + viaje (presencial o virtual).

7. Requisitos de la persona postulante

Básico

• Identificarse como persona trans (consultar el punto 5 anterior).

• Mínimo 3 años de activismo trans directo, idealmente a nivel regional y/o internacional.

• Tener reconocimiento de activistas trans de tu región como activista/líder comunitarie.

• Fluidez (oral y escrita) en inglés o español .

• Capaz y con disposición a trabajar en un entorno diverso (activistas y donantes).

• Pasaporte que permite viajar internacionalmente (para reuniones presenciales).

• Confiable en el cumplimiento de tareas y plazos.

• Experiencia en la gestión y presentación de informes sobre financiamientos para proyectos relacionados con personas trans.

8. Conflicto de intereses:
Las personas integrantes del PCA (y sus familiares directos) no podrán participar activamente en ningún grupo que solicite financiamiento al FIT durante su mandato, ni beneficiarse económicamente de los apoyos financieros del FIT ya concedidos o en curso ( véase la Política de Conflicto de Intereses de la FIT ). Ten en cuenta que, si formas parte de una organización o participas en ella y se te selecciona como integrante del PCA, dicha organización no podrá solicitar apoyos financieros durante su mandato.

9. Duración y remuneración

• Duración del mandato: Tres (3) años, designado por la Junta.

• Compensación:
1.500 dólares estadounidenses por ciclo anual de apoyos financieros, además de los gastos de viaje y dietas cubiertos para las reuniones del FIT.

10. Proceso de selección:
La junta designará a siete activistas, prestando especial atención a la diversidad de identidades y expresiones de género, así como a la inclusión de grupos más marginados dentro de las comunidades trans. Alentamos encarecidamente a hombres trans y personas trans masculinas a presentar su solicitud.

11. Cómo solicitar
Por favor, envía tu solicitud a través de BambooHR antes del 30 de noviembre de 2026.
Tenemos previsto informar a todas las personas postulantes de nuestras decisiones antes de enero de 2027.

postings.title: Senior Full Stack Engineer (Backend-oriented), Growth - Platform
postings.descriptionText:
About CookUnity :

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul.

Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About CookUnity

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul.
Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world.
If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About the Team:
Our Growth Platform team brings together Engagement and Accounts & Identity to build the experiences and technical foundations that help customers start, deepen, and renew their relationship with CookUnity .
On the Engagement side, we help new customers build lasting habits, keep active customers engaged, grow through referrals, and welcome back customers who have left. On the Accounts & Identity side, we own the services that power customer accounts, authentication, and secure access across our products, providing reliable capabilities that other engineering teams build upon.
Our work spans customer experiences across web and mobile, shared backend services, and the evolution of our platform into scalable, independent systems. We partner closely with Product, Design, Data, and Engineering to experiment, measure outcomes, and turn successful ideas into lasting capabilities. For engineers, this means combining direct customer impact with deep technical ownership, making CookUnity easier to use while helping teams across the company build and move faster.

The role:
As a Senior Full Stack Engineer (Backend oriented) on our Growth Platform team, you will help shape and own the core services behind Accounts & Identity, including authentication, user accounts, and the foundations of a shared notification system.
Working closely with our Staff Engineer, you will take ownership from technical design through implementation, rollout, and operation in production. You will evolve our authentication platform and User Service, build reliable integrations across services, and establish reusable capabilities that enable product teams to deliver timely, relevant notifications across channels.
This role calls for strong backend engineering expertise and sound judgment around distributed systems, database design, performance, and real-time and event-driven architectures. You should be comfortable investigating slow queries, designing APIs and asynchronous workflows, and making practical tradeoffs around consistency, scalability, security, and reliability.
You will partner with engineers across CookUnity to understand their needs and turn them into clear service boundaries and dependable integrations. Your impact will come from both delivering new capabilities and ensuring that the systems other teams depend on remain fast, observable, and easy to build upon.

Responsibilities:

• Own the design, implementation, and operation of core backend services across authentication, identity, and user account management.

• Partner with our Staff Engineer to define technical direction, make architecture decisions, and deliver projects from discovery through production.

• Build the foundations of a shared notification system, including event processing, delivery workflows, and integrations with messaging providers.

• Design APIs and service integrations with clear contracts, reliable failure handling, and well-defined ownership.

• Improve performance and scalability through database design, query optimization, indexing, caching, and efficient data access patterns.

• Build asynchronous and real-time capabilities, accounting for retries, idempotency, ordering, and data consistency.

• Evolve legacy functionality into independent services, planning safe migrations that preserve data integrity and service availability.

• Protect customer data through secure authentication, authorization, and access management practices.

• Establish meaningful automated tests, observability, and rollout strategies, and participate in incident response and the on-call rotation.

• Collaborate with Product and Engineering teams to translate business needs into reusable platform capabilities, review code, and mentor other engineers.

Qualifications:

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, with a strong focus on backend services and production systems.

• Strong backend development experience with both Kotlin/Java and Node.js with TypeScript, including building and operating production services. Deep expertise in at least one stack and the ability to contribute independently in the other.

• Solid knowledge of relational databases, including data modeling, indexing, query optimization, transactions, and safe schema migrations.

• Experience building distributed systems and asynchronous workflows, with an understanding of retries, idempotency, and data consistency.

• Experience diagnosing and improving backend performance using metrics, logs, traces, and profiling.

• Familiarity with authentication and authorization concepts, including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, and secure session management.

• Experience integrating internal services and third-party APIs, with thoughtful handling of failures and service dependencies.

• A track record of owning projects from technical design through testing, deployment, and production support.

• Clear communication skills, advanced English, and the ability to collaborate on technical decisions and explain tradeoffs.

Benefits

💸 Get paid in USD
🗺 Work remotely: design the life that you want
⛱ Enjoy 15 days of vacation each year from the start date

🎄 16 fully paid Argentinean holidays
🩺 Healthcare Benefit: Monthly stipend to use in your preferred healthcare provider
🗓️ 5- year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity , you get a 4-week paid sabbatical

🐣 Paid Family leave
🕯 Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises
🧘🏽‍♀️ Customize the benefits that suit your needs! Access a range of perks tailored to you, including learning opportunities, wellness memberships, delivery apps, and more through our comprehensive benefit platform
🤖 AI-forward workplace: enterprise access to ChatGPT and Claude to help you work smarter and grow faster.

🧑‍🏫 Personalized English coach

If you’re interested in this role, please submit your application, and if we think you might be a fit, we'll get in touch with you. Thank you for your time!

CookUnity is an Equal Opportunity Employer . We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or physical or mental disability.

A quick note for all candidates
We’ve recently seen an increase in recruitment scams across the industry, and we want to make sure you (and your data) stay safe while applying to CookUnity . We also want you to know that we take this seriously — sometimes, as part of our process, we may ask for a brief “proof of humanity” to confirm that we’re connecting with a real person, not an impersonator. Here are a few tips to help you protect yourself and know what to expect from us:

• Apply only through our official channels. All open roles are listed on our official careers page:

• Our recruiters are real people — and easy to verify. You can always find them on LinkedIn with verified profiles. If you’re unsure, feel free to reach out to us on our official LinkedIn Company Page.

• We only communicate through official CookUnity channels. That means emails ending in @cookunity.com and interviews held through official company platforms (Google Meet or Zoom) — never WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS.

• We’ll never ask for payment or personal financial details. If anyone does, please don’t share any information and let us know right away.

If something ever feels off or you’re unsure about a message, we’d much rather you double-check with us. You can always contact us directly through any of our social media channels. We appreciate your interest in joining CookUnity — and we care about keeping your experience (and safety) as genuine as possible.

What you will own

• The core angle, end to end. Research, concepts, scripts, briefs and the iteration loop, with a pod of editors assigned to you.

• Volume with a point. Around ten net-new concepts a week, plus the iterations that follow from what wins.

• The numbers. Hit rate and new-customer ROAS on your angle, read in Triple Whale, with a weekly view of what you tested, what won and why.

• The system. The testing framework for the angle, so the pod gets better every month rather than relying on inspiration.

• The people. Mentoring the strategists who join the pod after you, and setting the standard for briefs that editors can execute without going back and forth.

What this role is not
This is not a media buying role; our buyers run the accounts and you work with them daily. It is not an agency account seat with five clients, and it is not a brand or organic content role. You own one angle for one brand, deeply.

Who we are looking for

• You have owned creative strategy inside a DTC consumer brand, in supplements, wellness, consumer health or a similar category, on meaningful spend, and you can show the ads and the numbers behind them.

• You think in hooks, angles, formats and iterations, and you know the difference between a winner and a lucky launch.

• You have used AI video tools in production, or you are curious enough to learn ours fast.

What is hard about this
We would rather you hear it now than in month three:

• The volume is real. Ten net-new concepts a week with your editors is the job, not a stretch goal.

• The angle is mature. Most of the obvious ideas have been tested; the wins come from research, iteration and taste.

• Our CMO reviews the work closely and has strong opinions. You will need to defend yours with data.

• Priorities change quickly. We decide fast and expect the same from you.

Type

Full-time, independent contractor.

Very competitive, set with the person, with a performance bonus tied to spend and ROAS. We would rather hear your expectation than anchor you with a number.

Location
Remote. US, Europe or Latin America, with a working day that overlaps US Eastern hours.

Reports to

Our Head of Creative.

Team
A pod of dedicated video editors, with strategists joining the pod over time.

Start
As soon as possible, ideally December 2026.

Send us your CV or LinkedIn profile, plus short answers to three questions:

• The brand where you owned creative strategy. What was the spend, what was your hit rate, and which two or three ads are you proudest of? Links, please.

• Look at our ads in the Meta Ad Library. Which angle would you test next and why?

postings.title: Senior Full Stack Engineer (.NET/React) - AI Services
postings.descriptionText:
PROJECT OVERVIEW
Our client is building the software that hearing clinics run on patient records, bookings, hearing tests and sales. Clinic chains and hospitals use it every day. You join the team that owns the Sales domain: quote, invoice, insurance claim and payment. We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer who ships business outcomes, not just tickets. You own features end to end - from why a clinic needs them, through design and build, to checking in production that they worked. AI coding agents are a normal part of every step of your work.
Tech environment: C# / .NET 8.0, Azure Services (Azure SQL, AI Search, Service Bus, App Insights, Data Factory), Entity Framework Core, Docker, Kubernetes, MassTransit, React with TypeScript, plus growing use of Python for AI tooling and experimentation.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

• Design, build and run full-stack features in the Sales domain: .NET services, event-driven integrations and React front end.

• Work with the Product Owner and QA from discovery onwards. Shape the spec and agree acceptance criteria before code is written.

• Find the gaps in a spec before you build. Close the small ones yourself and bring only business questions to the Product Owner.

• Use AI tools across the whole lifecycle: planning, design, build, testing, review and maintenance. Keep the human judgement on correctness, security and data protection.

• Own quality: unit and integration tests, code review, and non-functional requirements (performance, security, observability) as part of the design.

• Follow features into production: watch telemetry and usage, support releases, investigate incidents and close the loop with the product team.

• Contribute to architecture discussions and decision records with the Tech Lead and architects and help pay down tech debt in the sales flows.

• Make the team better at AI: mentor engineers and share the instructions, checks and small tools that work.

Product Mindset
As AI takes on more of the typing, the value of an engineer moves to judgement: knowing what to build, why, and what good looks like for the user. In this role you:

• Start every feature with the business question: who in the clinic uses it, and what problem it solves for them.

• Push back with alternatives when a request is expensive and a simpler solution gives most of the value.

• Explain technical trade-offs in business terms to Product Owners, delivery and customer-facing colleagues.

• Look at usage, support tickets and customer feedback after release, and feed what you learn into the next iteration.

IF YOU ARE

• Typically 5+ years of software engineering experience , with a strong track record of building and running production systems. We value practical experience and demonstrated capabilities over years alone.

•
Strong hands-on experience with C# and modern .NET , including:

• Core and Web APIs.

• Entity Framework / Entity Framework Core.

• Clean Architecture and maintainable application design.

• Solid frontend development experience using React and TypeScript , particularly for complex business applications.

• Practical experience designing and developing microservices architectures .

•
Understanding of asynchronous communication and event-driven systems, ideally using:

•
Azure Service Bus.

•
MassTransit.

• Similar messaging and event-processing technologies.

• Strong SQL database experience, including relational data modelling and transactional business data.

• Experience with API design, automated testing, debugging, and security fundamentals.

•
Hands-on experience using AI coding agents as part of everyday development, such as:

• Ability to demonstrate practical AI-assisted development workflows, including examples of reviewing AI-generated code, identifying mistakes, and understanding when AI should not be used.

• Strong product mindset, with examples of contributing to feature definition, understanding business needs, and influencing technical and product decisions.

• Good command of English (B2 or above), both written and spoken.

NICE TO HAVE

• Python for AI tooling, evaluations and prototypes.

• Features built on LLM APIs: prompting, tool use, and measuring the quality of the results.

• Experience in regulated domains (medical devices, healthcare, finance) or with sensitive personal data.

•
AKS / Kubernetes.

• You have built or improved developer tooling, CI/CD or AI agent setups that other engineers use.

AS AN OPINOV8R, YOU WILL HAVE

• Digital-First Approach: Great talent knows no borders! You can work from wherever you are — we hire and collaborate with professionals worldwide.

• Remote Work Model: Balance your professional and personal life with our flexible working conditions, empowering you to deliver your best from anywhere.

• Exciting Projects: Dive into impactful projects across industries that challenge and spark creativity.

• Boost Your Expertise: Grow your career with continuous learning, development opportunities, and hands-on experience.

• Join the Best Team Ever: Collaborate with our diverse and cross-cultural team of passionate technologists and creative thinkers.

HOW’S THE HIRING PROCESS GOING
We strive to make our hiring process smooth and transparent to find the perfect match for both sides. Steps may differ depending on the role, but here’s what to expect:

• Initial Interview: If your background fits the role, we’ll invite you for an interview with a Talent Acquisition Specialist.

• Technical Interview: Depending on the position, you may complete a technical assessment or test task.

• Client's Interviews: 2 rounds

• Final Decision: After all steps, we’ll get back to you with the result and next steps.

Our Core Values

• Find a Better Way: We dig until we understand the real problem, then improve or innovate to solve it. Focused on the 20% that drives the biggest result.

• Have Each Other's Back: We work as a team. We support, step in, and go the extra mile to create a great experience for each other and our clients.

• Honor Your Word: We honor our promises, hold ourselves accountable, and do the right thing even when nobody’s looking.

• Own Your Growth: We're obsessed with personal growth and take pride in the work we deliver. Intrinsically motivated, we hold ourselves to a high standard and never coast.

• Bring Your A-Game: We take care of our recovery, health, and family time, and that’s why we show up focused, energized, and ready to perform at our best.

🎯 Role Overview
As an Engineering Manager, you will own the whole platform behind our product, back end and front end: everything that takes the data our data team publishes and puts it in front of every client. You make it reliable, fast, secure and worth what it costs, and you make sure we see a failure before a client does.
You are a strategic architect and an independent thinker who leads people well. You shape what we build, not just how: you question every request against the client's real need, propose the simplest design and avoid complexity that turns into debt. You lead a small team that uses AI to do more with less: we would rather have two great engineers using AI than a bigger team.
At least half your time is hands-on: architecture, design, reviewing code (including AI-written code) and building with AI agents. The rest is leading the team.

💡 Key Responsibilities

• Own the platform end to end. Design and evolve the architecture of our whole platform, back end and front end, that takes the data our data team publishes and serves it to every client. Write down each major decision and why, and remove old shortcuts instead of rebuilding them.

• Catch failures before clients do. Set up the alerts, testing and monitoring that surface problems before a client notices. After a serious failure, run a no-blame review, find the root cause (a missing test, alert, skill or owner) and fix it so it never repeats.

• Keep critical services up, fast and current. Run our critical services to clear targets for uptime and response time, and make sure every client gets newly published data within a day.

• Protect client data. Give every login only the access it needs, keep each client’s data apart, close security findings on time, and work with security specialists where it counts.

• Own cloud cost. Keep the platform bill within budget and bring the cost per paid client down every quarter, without slowing anything down.

• Challenge every request. Partner with Product to test each request against the client’s real need and its running cost, propose the simplest design, and put numbers on the tradeoffs. If Product uses 50 columns, we don’t serve 500.

postings.title: Performance Creative Editor (Contract)
postings.descriptionText:
We sell mushroom coffee direct to consumers. Paid ads on Meta and Google are how we grow, and the creative is the variable that decides whether it works. We test continuously and we measure what wins, so the feedback you get here is specific rather than taste-based.
Our creative strategists write the scripts and own the angle. You own the execution and, specifically, the first five seconds. You will ship 15 to 25 finished ads a month, deliberately fewer than most performance shops expect, because we would rather you spend the hours deciding what to change than cutting another variant nobody learns from.

What you will do

•
Cut paid ads for Meta and Google from scripts and angles handed to you by a strategist. Vertical, sound-on, short, fast-paced.

•
Own the hook. The script arrives written; the first five seconds are your call. We have firm views, built from our own account data, about which openers work for this product and which quietly kill a good ad. You will learn them in week one, apply them without being asked, and argue when one is wrong.

•
Iterate winners, not only originate. Most of your month is making something that already works work harder, which in our testing beats originating from scratch by a wide margin.

•
Build variants that change one thing on purpose. We have burned whole quarters on same-day copies that duplicated instead of testing. A variant that teaches us nothing is worse than no variant.

•
Read your own numbers. You get access to our creative analytics and attribution tools, and your output is measured. You bring reads to the weekly creative review rather than waiting to be told what lost.

Requirements

What we are looking for
Three or more years cutting ads that ran on a paid account. We care about what you have shipped, not your title.

Required

•
Paid ads as the spine of your work. You can name a brand that spent money distributing something you cut.

•
A performance number you personally moved on a specific piece of creative, before and after.

•
You know which metrics decide and which mislead. An ad is judged on spend and acquisition cost over its first week, not on thumbstop or hold rate. Plenty of good editors optimise for retention and engagement because those are the numbers they are shown. We will ask you which metrics you have actually been held to and what you think they do and do not predict. There is a right answer and it is not the obvious one.

•
AI creation, fluently and invisibly. Generative tooling is how you hit variant volume at this cadence: image and video generation, voice, upscaling, automated captioning and reframing. The bar is output nobody can tell was generated. We are not buying AI-looking content, we are buying your speed.

•
Premiere or DaVinci to a professional standard , plus After Effects or CapCut. You finish your own sound.

• English good enough to argue with a media buyer about why a hook is wrong.

• Your own machine, reliable internet, a quiet place to take a call.

Strongly preferred

• Supplements, wellness, beverage, beauty or DTC subscription. Our claims language is regulated.

• Range across the formats direct response actually runs on: offer-led creative, objection and confession openers, and one person talking to camera. Tell us which you are strongest in.

• Creative analytics tooling such as Motion, Triple Whale or Northbeam.

• Cutting from creator and UGC footage, including the unglamorous work of making mediocre raw material perform.

Not required: a degree, a cinematic showreel, agency names on your resume, or managing anyone.

Before you apply
We decline a lot of genuinely skilled editors who have never cut a direct-response ad. That wastes everyone's time, so, plainly:
Not a fit if your portfolio is mainly corporate or internal communications, brand films, weddings and events, news or broadcast, documentary, event recaps and sizzle reels, music videos, real estate, podcast production, long-form YouTube, or B2B training. Those are real crafts and close to the opposite problem: a beautiful 90-second brand film and an ad that holds a stranger for three seconds and sells coffee are not the same skill.
The test: can you name a brand that paid to distribute something you cut, and the metric you were judged on? If the honest answer is that you have made great videos but nobody bought media against them, this seat will not work, and we would rather say so now than after two interviews.
One more thing. A cover letter that repeats this posting back to us reads exactly as it sounds. Tell us about your work instead.

Benefits

Engagement
Independent contractor, ongoing, invoiced monthly. Not employment.

Location
Remote, anywhere in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, or Uruguay. You are responsible for your own taxes and any local registration.

Hours
Async by default. We ask for 2-3 hours of daily overlap with Austin, Texas (Central Time) for the creative review and buyer conversations. You choose which hours.

Commitment
Full-time equivalent effort. We are not looking for someone fitting this between three other clients.

Equipment
Yours. We provide software seats (Adobe CC, Motion, Frame.io) and all footage, product and creator assets.

Start

As soon as the right person is found.

You'll take a clinician's 90-second explanation of how GLP-1s work and make it land. You'll turn a customer's iPhone testimonial into a Meta ad that converts. On spec, on time, and on the right side of compliance.
This is not a generalist editing role. You'll be cutting healthcare content in a tightly regulated category (compounded medications, metabolic health, HRT). Every cut, every overlay, every text card has to be both watchable and compliant. Paid ads in this space get extra scrutiny from Meta, TikTok, and the FTC, so you'll work closely with our social media manager, healthcare creators, and compliance reviewer to make sure everything ships clean.
The right person is fast, opinionated about what makes short-form work, and fluent with modern AI editing tools. You're also detail-oriented enough to catch when a stray B-roll clip, an AI voiceover, or a misplaced caption could create a compliance problem. No healthcare background required (we'll train you), but you do need to care about getting it right.

What You'll Do

Educational content (organic)

• Edit 12–16 short-form educational videos per month (15–90 seconds) from self-shot creator footage for Instagram Reels and TikTok

• Add captions, lower thirds, callouts, on-screen text, and B-roll where it strengthens the message

Paid ads

• Cut 8–15 paid ad variations per month for Meta, TikTok, and YouTube: hook-led, conversion-focused, built for testing

• Produce multiple variants of each concept (different hooks, CTAs, and first-3-second openers) so the media team can run proper creative tests

• Iterate quickly on winning ads: recut hooks, swap B-roll, refresh creative when fatigue sets in

UGC

• Edit UGC submissions from real customers and paid UGC creators into polished short-form content that still feels native and authentic (not over-produced)

• Stitch multi-clip UGC into cohesive narratives (problem, product, result framing, within compliance bounds)

Across all streams

• Use AI tools strategically to speed up production (auto-captioning, transcript-based editing, B-roll generation, voice cleanup) without letting AI shortcuts compromise accuracy or compliance

• Apply LumiMeds brand standards consistently: fonts, colors, logo placement, end cards, disclosure formatting

• Implement compliance reviewer feedback on cuts and revisions, sometimes across multiple rounds

• Maintain organized project files and an archive of raw footage, approved B-roll, finished cuts, and ad variant trees

• Stay current on what's working on Reels, TikTok, and paid social in the health and wellness space

What You Won't Do

• You will NOT write scripts or determine clinical content — that comes from our licensed creators and the marketing team

• You will NOT add efficacy claims, weight-loss promises, or outcome language in captions, on-screen text, or ad copy

• You will NOT use AI to generate fake clinician footage, deepfake any creator or customer, clone voices, or fabricate B-roll that misrepresents what's being described

• You will NOT use before/after imagery, testimonial framings, or comparisons to branded products (Wegovy, Ozempic, Zepbound, Mounjaro)

• You will NOT upload, publish, or push final files live to ad accounts — final files go to the social media manager and media buyer

What We're Looking For

Required

• 2+ years editing short-form vertical video for social. Portfolio with current work required

• Demonstrated experience editing paid social ads (Meta, TikTok, or YouTube) — not just organic content. You understand hook-led structure, retention curves, and why ad creative is different from organic creative

• Strong fluency in at least one of: Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, or CapCut Pro

• Working knowledge of AI editing tools: Descript or similar transcript-based editing, AI captioning (CapCut, Submagic, Opus Clip), AI audio cleanup (Adobe Enhance, Auphonic)

• Comfort cutting UGC: taking imperfect, multi-source footage and making it work without stripping out the authenticity that makes UGC perform

• Captioning skills that go beyond auto-generated: accurate, well-timed, well-styled, readable on mute

• Genuine taste for what makes short-form work: pacing, hooks, retention, when to cut, when to let a beat breathe

• Willingness to learn FDA marketing compliance basics as they apply to compounded medications and paid health advertising (we'll train you)

Strongly Preferred

• Direct experience editing paid DTC ads in healthcare, wellness, supplements, telehealth, or other regulated, performance-driven categories

• Familiarity with the visual language differences between educational, UGC, and ad content

• Experience producing ad variant trees (same concept, multiple hooks, CTAs, and openers) for systematic creative testing

• Experience working with a brand kit and maintaining visual consistency across many cuts

• Motion graphics chops: clean text animations, simple lower thirds, callout treatments

• Comfort with audio cleanup (noise reduction, leveling, music ducking)

• Experience using AI tools responsibly in regulated contexts

• Working knowledge of Meta, TikTok, and YouTube ad creative specs and policy (especially health and wellness ad policies)

Bonus

• Color grading skills beyond basic correction

• Spanish or Tagalog fluency (we're planning bilingual content and matching captioning helps)

• Experience with AI dubbing or translation tools (ElevenLabs, HeyGen, Rask) for bilingual ad and content workflows

• Experience editing for accounts or ad accounts in the 100K+ follower or six-figure monthly ad spend range

Logistics

•
Engagement type: Full-time (W-2)

•
Location: Fully remote, U.S.-based preferred (open to Canada/Latin America for the right person)

•
Software: You bring your own. We'll cover any LumiMeds -specific tools, plugins, or AI tool subscriptions

•
Start date: As soon as the right person is found

What Working With Us Looks Like

• Footage and briefs drop into a shared folder: educational footage from creators, UGC from customers and paid UGC creators, raw assets for ad concepts

• Each project comes with a brief: format, platform, aspect ratios needed, hook variations to produce, compliance considerations flagged upfront

• You cut, deliver a first version (or variant set), and post to a review thread

• You revise (usually 1–2 rounds for organic, sometimes 3+ for ads where compliance is stricter)

• Final files get approved, you upload to the delivery folder, marketing and media buying take it from there

• Weekly check-in during high-volume ad pushes; monthly check-in (30 min) otherwise

How to Apply
Send the following to :

• A short note (3–5 sentences) on why this role interests you

• Your reel or 3–5 links to recent work, ideally a mix of organic short-form, UGC edits, and paid ads

• At least one example of a paid ad you edited, with a sentence on what platform it ran on and what the goal was

• A sentence or two on which AI tools you actually use in your workflow and what for

• Your rate expectations (per-video, per-variant, or monthly retainer)

• Software you cut on

• If you have it: an example of a piece you edited for a regulated category and a sentence on what constraints you were editing under

We review applications on a rolling basis. Expect to hear back within 2 weeks if there's a fit.

Why This Role Exists
LumiMeds runs three video streams that all live or die on the same craft: educational content that earns trust, UGC that proves real people use the product, and paid ads that bring new patients in the door. They look different, they perform on different metrics, and they each have their own compliance traps. We need one editor who can move between all three without losing the plot.
AI tools have made parts of this faster than ever. They've also made it easier than ever to ship something polished, plausible, and quietly wrong — especially in paid ads. We need someone who can use modern tools to move fast, and never let the polish drift into territory that compromises the brand, the creators we work with, or the audience's trust.

How to Apply

If this role sounds like a fit, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your application in English and ensure your resume reflects relevant experience for the role.

This position is open to candidates based in approved locations, depending on the role and business needs. Qualified applicants will be contacted for next steps.

LumiMeds is an equal opportunity employer. We hire based on skills, experience, and alignment with our values.

Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

***Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.

A day in the life:
As a Creative Quality & Compliance Specialist , you’ll play an integral part in the overall quality and regulatory integrity of creative output across the Healthcare division, serving as the quality and compliance checkpoint within the creative production workflow. In this role, you’ll report directly to the Creative department and work alongside Creative Project Managers who own delivery timelines and task trafficking.
You will act as the gate through which every piece of creative passes before it reaches client Medical, Legal, and Regulatory (MLR) reviewers and again before it goes live. You'll review ads, landing pages, emails, social content, and video for MLR regulatory compliance, brand and design standards, and copy accuracy. Additionally, you’ll operate hands-on inside Veeva Vault PromoMats—managing claims, annotations, references, and submission packages—while building and refining the quality standards the creative team works against to raise the bar across the healthcare portfolio.
While your primary authority is quality and compliance, you’ll also support the creative production workflow by maintaining deliverable trackers, coordinating feedback cycles with client stakeholders, and trafficking tasks between the creative team and client POCs. As the Creative Project Manager and Account PM lead delivery management at scale, you will keep the creative lane organized and moving while ensuring nothing ships that shouldn’t.

Key Responsibilities:

• Pre-Submission Compliance QA: Review all creative assets against MLR requirements — claims accuracy, fair balance, ISI placement, reference linking, branded vs. unbranded vs. disease-awareness rules — before they enter client Medical, Legal, and Regulatory review.

• Post-Approval Launch QA: Final quality proof of approved assets — landing pages, ads, emails, creative — before they go live, confirming that approved content was implemented correctly and no errors were introduced in production.

• Veeva Vault PromoMats Operations: Own the hands-on Veeva workflow — annotating assets, entering and linking claims, managing references, tracking submission status, and packaging 2253 filings.

• Brand & Design Standards Enforcement: Review creative output for visual consistency, spec adherence, and style guide compliance across all healthcare client deliverables.

• Copy Quality Review: Review all copy for grammar, tone, messaging accuracy, and alignment with approved claims and client brand voice.

• QA Process Documentation & Refinement: Build, maintain, and continuously improve the quality and compliance standards, checklists, and review processes the creative team follows.

• Creative Workflow Coordination: Support creative production operations alongside the Creative Project Manager and Account PM — maintaining Asana boards and deliverable trackers, communicating timelines and managing feedback cycles with client stakeholders, trafficking tasks between the creative team and client POCs, coordinating with cross-channel PMs on shared deliverables, and organizing client-provided assets within Power Digital’s file structure.

• Employ AI technologies to enhance and optimize business processes.

• Utilize and leverage Power Digital’s Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department.

• Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements:

• 4+ years in healthcare or pharmaceutical creative production, agency or in-house, with direct exposure to MLR review workflows

• Demonstrated understanding of FDA OPDP guidance and 21 CFR 202, including fair balance, ISI placement, branded vs. unbranded vs. disease-awareness content rules, and 2253 filing requirements

• Veeva Vault PromoMats experience (annotating, claims management, submission tracking) highly preferred

• Strong eye for brand consistency, design quality, and copy accuracy across digital formats (paid social, display, landing pages, email)

• Process-oriented with the ability to document, maintain, and improve QA standards without external direction

• Comfortable reviewing and providing clear, actionable feedback on creative work from designers, copywriters, and freelancers

• Proficiency with Asana or comparable project management platforms

• Experience working alongside project management teams in a fast-paced agency environment

• Bonus: Veeva PromoMats certification, experience with modular content strategies, or prior work across both pharma-regulated and non-regulated healthcare clients

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

• First-pass approval rate: 80%+ of assets cleared by client M/L/R reviewers on first submission

• QA turnaround time: internal reviews completed within defined SLA (e.g. 24–48 hours)

• Pre-launch error rate: <2% of launched assets requiring post-launch correction

• 100% accuracy on 2253 filings and regulatory submission packaging

• Documented QA standards maintained and current across all supported accounts

Most Important Things (MITs)

• Establish the pre-submission and pre-launch QA checkpoints as defined, repeatable stages in the creative workflow.

• Own the Veeva PromoMats workflow for assigned accounts — claims, annotations, references, and submissions operating cleanly from day one.

• Build and maintain the QA standards documentation (checklists, compliance reference guides, brand review criteria) the creative team works against.

• Develop a working rhythm with Creative Project Managers so that QA is a checkpoint in the pipeline, not a bottleneck.

Benefits & Perks:

• Base salary paid in USD + commission opportunities

• Unlimited Time Off available on day one

• Fully flex work environment: full-remote, in-office, or hybrid

• Healthcare stipend: $50/month to support your healthcare or insurance costs

• National Holidays + 2 Mental Health Recharge Days per year

• Unlimited opportunities for growth & leadership within a rapidly growing firm

• Ongoing employee development programs for personal and professional growth (Hedgehog and Vital 5s)

• Quarterly awards including prize money and recognition for outstanding performance

• Opportunities to be involved in company DEI initiatives

Power Digital’s people and culture are at the core of our success, which is why diversity in our team’s backgrounds and experiences are paramount. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employees' points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Power Digital does NOT charge any application, processing, or training fee at any stage of the recruitment or hiring process. All genuine job openings will be posted on our careers page at . Ververica is the original creator of Apache Flink® and remains a core contributor to it. Flink is the leading open-source engine for stream and batch processing. It runs mission-critical workloads at Netflix, Alibaba, Amazon and Uber, as well as at banks, telcos and global enterprises.

We build Ververica Unified Streaming Data Platform, an enterprise-grade platform for real-time data on top of Flink. Backed by one of the world's largest tech companies, we combine open-source innovation with long-term stability.

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS
We are hiring a Technical Account Manager (TAM) to be the technical lead for our customers across North and South America. You will be their trusted advisor and hands-on partner, from first deployment through long-term production operations.

You will work with platform owners, data engineers and architects to design, run and scale their stream processing on Ververica Unified Streaming Data Platform. Because you work in their time zone, you will be the person they reach first when something matters, during the sales process and after it.

When you are not with customers, you will deepen your Flink expertise, feed what you learn back into our products, and help grow the Flink community.
WHAT YOU BRING

• 3+ years in a customer-facing technical role such as TAM, Solutions Engineer, Solutions Architect or Support Engineer.

• Hands-on Kubernetes experience. Our product runs on Kubernetes, so this is essential.

• Experience with at least one major public cloud (AWS, Azure or Google Cloud).

• Ability to read and reason about Java code, working knowledge of Java 11+ and a basic understanding of the JVM.

• Working knowledge of SQL, including querying streaming data.

• Experience with distributed data processing or streaming systems such as Apache Flink, Apache Kafka, Apache Spark or Redpanda.

• Proven ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues under time pressure.

• Ability to manage several accounts and projects at once, set priorities and meet deadlines.

• Clear written and spoken English. You are comfortable with both engineers and executives.

NICE TO HAVE

• Experience running Apache Flink in production, or contributions to open-source data infrastructure projects.

• Working knowledge of Python, useful for customers on PyFlink.

• Experience with observability tools such as Grafana, Prometheus, Datadog or Dynatrace.

• Familiarity with DevOps workflows and CI/CD tooling in cloud-native environments.

• Spanish or Portuguese, for customers in Latin America.

LOCATION AND WORKING HOURS

This is a remote role for someone based between UTC-4 and UTC-7. That covers US and Canadian Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific time, plus Latin American countries in the same range.

• Your core hours follow your customers' business day in the Americas.

• A few early mornings each week overlap with our EMEA team for handovers and escalations.

• Occasional travel to customer sites and events, within North and South America.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Own the technical relationship with a portfolio of enterprise customers in the Americas, from onboarding through renewal and expansion.

• Guide customers in designing and optimizing their stream processing architecture on Ververica Unified Streaming Data Platform.

• Advise on Flink job design, deployment models (on-premises Kubernetes, public cloud, managed service, Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC)) and monitoring strategy.

• Troubleshoot and tune pipelines, connectors and clusters, and identify weak spots in customer architectures before they cause incidents.

• Lead incident triage and root cause analysis for your accounts, and build operational playbooks that help customers run Flink at scale.

• Support migrations from legacy or batch-based systems to real-time processing.

• Support pre-sales with technical discovery, proofs of concept and architecture reviews alongside the Sales team.

• Run regular check-ins and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) with strategic customers to align on goals, feedback and roadmap priorities.

• Act as the customer's voice to Engineering and Product, and work with Sales and Marketing on account plans.

• Hand over cleanly to EMEA colleagues so customers get continuous coverage across time zones.

• Join the on-call support rotation.

• Represent Ververica in customer meetings and roadmap sessions and, if you like, at conferences and meetups.

WHAT WE OFFER

• Competitive compensation: salary, equity and performance bonus

Overview

•
World Business Lenders (WBL) is a privately held portfolio lender specializing in real estate-secured business loans for underserved businesses. WBL operates with a fully remote, multinational workforce and an experienced executive leadership team.

• Typically, the work schedule is from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, though additional hours may be required based on business needs.

About the Role

• The Valuation Quality Control/Review Appraiser will serve as a subject matter expert in residential or commercial real estate appraisal. The role is responsible for reviewing appraisals and other valuation reports prepared by internal analysts and third-party providers, identifying material deficiencies, and recommending property values to the appropriate committee.

• This position is focused on appraisal review, quality control, collateral risk assessment, and communication of clear, supportable valuation recommendations. It also entails producing appraisals from start to finish.

What Success Looks Like

• Consistently delivers accurate, timely, and defensible valuation recommendations.

• Identifies material appraisal deficiencies and effectively communicates collateral risks.

• Provides clear, well-supported recommendations to credit and investment committees.

• Maintains high-quality, consistent appraisal review standards and supports junior analysts.

What You'll Be Doing (Core Responsibilities)

• Review residential or commercial appraisals, evaluations, broker price opinions, automated valuation models, inspections, and related valuation reports.

• Assess the accuracy, completeness, credibility, and suitability of each report for its intended use.

• Evaluate property characteristics, highest and best use, zoning, market conditions, comparable selection, adjustments, income assumptions, capitalization rates, cost estimates, and value reconciliation.

• Identify unsupported assumptions, mathematical errors, stale data, weak comparables, excessive adjustments, material omissions, and other valuation deficiencies.

• Return deficient reports for correction, clarification, or additional support.

• Develop an independent recommendation of property value based on the appraisal, supporting market evidence, internal records, inspections, and other available information.

• Recommend acceptance, modification, rejection, or further investigation of submitted valuation conclusions.

• Prepare concise written summaries of findings, risks, and recommended values.

• Present valuation recommendations to Investment Committee, Asset Resolution Committee, Initial Credit Review Committee or other decision-making committees.

• Explain valuation methodology, assumptions, market evidence, and collateral risks to management and committee members.

• Recommend additional appraisals, inspections, environmental reports, engineering studies, or other analysis when existing information is insufficient.

• Review work completed by junior analysts and provide technical guidance on appraisal methodology, comparable analysis, adjustments, and report documentation.

Requirements

• Education

• Bachelor’s degree in real estate, finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related field.

• Required Experience

• 7+ years of experience in real estate appraisal, appraisal review, collateral valuation, underwriting, credit, asset management, or a related field.

• Demonstrated experience reviewing both residential and commercial real estate appraisals.

• Strong knowledge of the sales comparison, income capitalization, and cost approaches.

• Experience evaluating comparable selection, market adjustments, income and expense assumptions, capitalization rates, highest and best use, and value reconciliation.

• Experience with distressed, transitional, nonperforming, foreclosed, or complex real estate.

• Strong analytical, written, verbal, and presentation skills.

• Ability to exercise independent judgment and challenge unsupported valuation conclusions.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, public records, property databases, listing platforms, mapping systems, and market research tools.

• State Certified General Real Estate Appraiser credential.

• MAI, SRA, AI-GRS, ASA, MRICS, or another recognized appraisal designation.

• Key Performance Measures

• Accuracy and defensibility of valuation recommendations

• Quality and timeliness of appraisal reviews

• Identification of material appraisal deficiencies

• Consistency with appraisal review standards

• Quality of committee presentations and written recommendations

• Variance between recommended values and subsequent transaction outcomes

• Remote Work Requirements

• Stable, reliable internet connection.

• Professional and dedicated remote working environment.

• Preferred Background / Industry Experience

• Real estate appraisal or appraisal review, particularly residential and commercial properties.

• Commercial real estate lending, mortgage lending, credit underwriting, or collateral risk management.

• Asset management, special assets, distressed debt, foreclosure, or REO involving complex or transitional real estate.

• Experience with portfolio lenders, banks, private credit, or other financial institutions.

• Experience supporting credit/investment committees, loan workouts, property dispositions, or other decisions involving real estate collateral.

• Key Soft Skills

• Strong analytical judgment and professional skepticism.

• Confidence to challenge appraisers, analysts, and internal stakeholders when conclusions are not adequately supported.

• Ability to make sound decisions when property information is incomplete or conflicting.

• Clear and concise written and verbal communication.

• Ability to explain complex valuation issues to non-appraisers and senior executives.

• Strong attention to detail without losing sight of the overall collateral risk.

• Comfortable defending a valuation recommendation in a committee environment.

• Collaborative coaching style when reviewing the work of junior analysts.

• High degree of independence, integrity, and objectivity

• Specific Technical Skills Needed

• Expert understanding of residential and commercial real estate appraisal.

• Strong command of the Sales Comparison and Income Capitalization approach.

• Ability to critically evaluate comparable selection and appraisal adjustments.

• Ability to analyze rents, operating expenses, NOI, capitalization rates, discount rates, and income-based valuations.

• Strong understanding of highest and best use, zoning, property condition, marketability, and location considerations.

• Ability to identify appraisal errors, unsupported assumptions, inconsistencies, and material data gaps.

• Experience reviewing distressed, nonperforming, foreclosed, transitional, or otherwise complex collateral preferred.

• Working knowledge of USPAP and applicable appraisal independence and regulatory standards.

• Proficiency with Excel, public property records, MLS/listing information, mapping tools, commercial real estate databases, and other valuation research resources.

postings.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
postings.descriptionText:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

•
Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

•
Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.

•
Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•
Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.

•
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.

•
Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.

•
Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.

•
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.

•
Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

•
You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.

•
You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.

•
You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.

•
You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.

•
You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.

•
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.

• Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

• "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.

• You want to be told what to do this week.

• You need a ticketing system to know what matters.

• You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting
This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

postings.title: Senior Officer, Conserving the Pantanal and Gran Chaco Wildlands
postings.descriptionText:
POSITION DESCRIPTION

THE PEW CHARITABLE TRUSTS
Senior Officer, Conserving the Pantanal and Gran Chaco Wildlands
(Protected Area Management and Conservation Finance)
The Environment Portfolio at The Pew Charitable Trusts
For more than 30 years, Pew has been a major force in engaging the public and policy makers about the causes, consequences, and solutions to some of the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. Our environment work spans all seven continents with more than 250 professionals working at the local, national, and international levels to reduce the scope and severity of global environmental problems, such as the erosion of large natural ecosystems that contain a great part of the world’s remaining biodiversity, and the destruction of the marine environment. Pew’s global environmental program focuses on science-based, nonpartisan, and sustainable solutions to help protect the planet and people. We work in partnership with governments, Indigenous rights holders, intergovernmental organizations, non-governmental organizations, local stakeholders, scientists, and other researchers to advance public policy so that nature and communities can thrive.
Since 1990, Pew has worked in North America, South America and Australia to protect large and critically important terrestrial ecosystems, including rivers and other freshwater resources, coastal temperate rainforests, interior mountain ranges, the northern boreal forests, Australia’s Outback, and Chilean Patagonia. We work to ensure these natural systems remain bountiful, functioning, and resilient, providing essential ecological services such as clean air and clean water, sustenance and food security for local communities and more broadly for the welfare of current and future generations. Our work relies on the sciences of conservation, sociology, biology, and economics to advocate for practical and durable solutions to the loss of biodiversity.
In the sea, reforms to how our oceans are managed are essential to address overfishing, pollution, and loss of habitat. Pew began its oceans program in the United States, focusing on ending overfishing and protecting fragile marine habitat. Starting in 2005, Pew’s ocean conservation program expanded around the world and played a significant role in reforming marine fisheries management in the European Union and on the high seas and creating large scale marine reserves around the world. Our work is grounded in the best available science and pursues domestic and international conservation measures that are long-term and provide permanent, durable protections for marine ecosystems. We also work to address systemic threats to the ocean, including from plastics, over-and-illegal fishing, seabed mining, and climate change.

Conserving the Pantanal and Gran Chaco Wildlands
South America’s Pantanal and Gran Chaco regions are among the most ecologically significant tropical wetlands and dry forests on Earth. This area spans parts of Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, and Argentina and contains thousands of plant and animal species and provides vital aquatic habitat, nutrient renewal, migration routes, and flood control for millions of animals and people living downstream. The region’s extensive ecosystems are currently threatened by deforestation, drought and intensification of wildfires related to climate change, and thus urgently need conservation action.
The project works with the policy framework in each country to solidify and expand protection of the extraordinary biodiversity of the Pantanal-Gran Chaco region. Pew partners with local and international conservation organizations, government agencies, and Indigenous governments and organizations to improve management of and expand protected areas, support Indigenous organizations and communities in the management of their territories, promote sustainable management for ranching lands, and to advance long-term conservation financing mechanisms for durable protections.

Position Overview
Reporting to the Project Director, Conserving the Pantanal and Gran Chaco Wildlands, the Senior Officer will lead efforts to develop long-term financing and improve the management of protected and conserved areas in the Pantanal-Gran Chaco landscape.
The Senior Officer will focus on identifying and pursuing finance, conservation, community development, and fundraising goals that support improved management of protected and conserved lands in the region. This will include collaboration with consultants, partners, government officials and other key stakeholders, as well as facilitating the project’s engagement in public policy and advocacy related to conservation finance and improved management. This position requires demonstrated leadership in public or private sector organizations focused on promoting sustainability and conservation.
The Senior Officer will be located either in Santa Cruz, Bolivia; or elsewhere within the South America region following evaluation by Pew.
Responsibilities for the Pantanal-Gran Chaco Project:

• Foster a work environment that inspires excellence, values impact, encourages transparency, builds mutual trust and respect, embraces and values diversity, and is collaborative, caring and compassionate. Under the Project Director’s leadership, manage aspects of Pew’s Pantanal-Gran Chaco initiative related to improving the management of the region’s protected and conserved areas. This includes organizing and coordinating high-level meetings, commissioning and conducting research, and managing strategic partnerships.

• In collaboration with relevant Pew staff and senior management, assess opportunities to expand or develop new financing strategies for protected and conserved areas in Bolivia, Brazil, and Argentina.

• Coordinate the development of priority financing initiatives in collaboration with Pew’s Pantanal and Gran Chaco team, consultants, and in-country partners.

• Provide technical guidance to Pew’s Pantanal and Gran Chaco team on financing frameworks, sustainable financing mechanisms, public resource allocation, and effective management.

• Support the Project Director in establishing and cultivating strategic alliances and launching joint initiatives with international organizations, foundations, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), government agencies, Indigenous organizations, and other institutions in the region.

• Promote best practices and innovations in protected area management and conservation in the Pantanal Gran-Chaco through public policy engagements and outreach efforts.

• Prepare regular updates for senior management and other audiences summarizing the initiative’s efforts and achievements toward financial sustainability of the region’s protected and conserved lands.

• Lead analysis and research within the framework of the Pantanal and Gran Chaco strategy to gather scientific, policy, and technical information on protected area conservation lands finances and management in Latin America.

• Represent Pew in external events online and in person, including meetings with national and local governments, multilateral organizations, and other institutions.

• Participate in activities that support program and Pew-wide objectives.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree in public policy, economics, business, natural resources management or related studies preferred.

• Generally, a minimum of 10 years

• Fluency in both English and Spanish is required, competence in Portuguese is desired.

• Significant experience in project management, financial mechanisms, and government engagement.

• Experience working with local and regional governments.

• Experience in the management of protected areas or other forms of conservation lands, including development of management plans, monitoring systems, and staff training programs.

• Acute political awareness and understanding of issues from a non-partisan perspective.

• Demonstrated experience building relationships across individuals and organizations with a range of interests and perspectives.

• Capacity to lead group discussions with individuals working in different roles and countries; skilled in training and guiding team members with a high degree of cultural sensitivity.

• Demonstrated experience meeting deadlines and effectively developing and moving projects forward with a high degree of independence and autonomy.

• Effective professional writing skills in both English and Spanish. Effectively communicates ideas, thoughts and concepts clearly and concisely and in a compelling way, both written and orally.

Travel
Travel up to 25% of the time to cities and remote locations in Bolivia, Brazil, Argentina and throughout Latin America, and to the United States as necessary.

Work Authorization
Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the country for which they are seeking employment without visa sponsorship.

Salary Range
The salary range represents a reasonable estimate of the annual salary based on Pew’s commitment to provide equitable and market-competitive pay. The actual salary offered will take into consideration many factors including but not limited to job-related knowledge, skills and experience, internal pay equity, and business need.

Total Rewards
This position offers a competitive salary and benefit program.
Pew is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions without regard to race, ethnicity, gender, or any other protected characteristics.
